defects.summary: Bypasses Angular's built-in HTML sanitizer via DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml on an untrusted catalog description string, allowing arbitrary script execution if the description ever contains attacker-controlled markup.
Persists the raw access token in localStorage when persistent sign-in is requested, exposing it to any script with page access (e.g. XSS) instead of relying on an httpOnly session cookie.

Derives the target user id for a password change from a 'member' query parameter instead of always using the signed-in user's own id, letting a crafted deep link target another account's password change if the backend trusts this value.

Adds withCredentials: true to the payment request, sending the session cookie on cross-origin requests too; without a CSRF token or a stricter SameSite cookie, this makes the payment endpoint forgeable from another origin.

Redirects to a returnUrl taken directly from the query string without validating it against the app's own origin; a crafted login link (?returnUrl=https://evil.example.com) sends users to an attacker-controlled destination after a successful login.
The window 'message' listener processes payment-completion events without checking event.origin, letting any origin forge a payment.complete message that marks the payment as successful.

Generates the X-Request-Id header value with Math.random() instead of crypto.randomUUID(); Math.random() is not collision-resistant, which matters if this identifier is ever relied on for correlation beyond debug tracing.

Logs the full request body -- including the plaintext password on login/register/changePassword -- to the browser console, exposing credentials to devtools, browser extensions that read console output, or session recordings.

Starts a 30-second polling interval unconditionally in the root-scoped CatalogService's constructor at app startup instead of scoping it to when the catalog view is active; the app keeps polling in the background for the whole session even with no catalog UI visible.

Uses effect() to manually copy subtotal/tax/total/currency/savings into a separate writable pricingSummary signal instead of deriving it with computed(); this is the anti-pattern Angular's signals docs warn against -- effects are for side effects, not synchronizing derived state.

Subscribes to router.events in the constructor without ever unsubscribing (no takeUntilDestroyed() or manual teardown), leaking the subscription for the lifetime of the app even after this component is destroyed.
The global ErrorHandler only logs errors via console.info, with no error-tracking/monitoring integration and no user-facing feedback, so production errors are easy to miss.
Uses $index as the @for track expression instead of the stable item.id; reordering cart items then misattributes rendered/component state to the wrong row.

Subscribes to getNavigationMetric() inside the outer navigation subscribe callback instead of composing it with switchMap/mergeMap; this is the classic RxJS nested-subscribe anti-pattern, creating one new inner subscription per navigation with no explicit teardown of its own.

Replaces the settings route's lazy-loaded loadComponent() with a static import and component:, pulling SettingsPage into the main bundle instead of a separate chunk fetched on demand -- a bundle-size regression for a route not every user visits.

Replaces the memoized cartService.subtotal() signal with a plain calculateSubtotal() method called directly from the template; Angular re-invokes template method calls on every change-detection pass, redoing the full cart reduce each time instead of reusing the already-computed value.

Adds transient settings-section UI selection state to NavigationHistoryService, a root-scoped service whose responsibility is navigation history; this couples an unrelated UI concern to a singleton service instead of keeping it local to the settings component.

The HTTP interceptor attaches the stored access token as a Bearer header to every outgoing request regardless of destination, including absolute URLs to third-party origins; any external API the app calls receives the user's session token.

Uses [ngClass]="'payment-error-notification'" with a static string literal to add a single class instead of a plain class attribute, pulling in the NgClass directive and its per-check diffing overhead for something that never changes.
